items.title: Mona Hinton interviewed by Milt Fillius and Michael Woods, Scottsdale, Arizona, March 4, 1995
items.q: to the day he died he would never call me anything but Mrs. Hinton. I used to say “Pops, it’s embarrassing, you call all the other wives by their first names,”

ctx.x: Well didn’t he live in the same neighborhood?

Not too far from us. He lived closer to LaGuardia Airport than we did. But and you know to the day he died he would never call me anything but Mrs. Hinton. I used to say “Pops, it’s embarrassing, you call all the other wives by their first names,” and one day he said to me and I said “why — it’s embarrassing to me that you always say ‘Mrs. Hinton.’” And he says, with that gravel voice, he said, “you have a baby, you’re a lady, I can’t call you anything but Mrs. Hinton.” And this was typical of him.
I want to ask you a question about him because I was teaching about him in my History of Jazz class. Tell us about his tone.
